notes:
Manga read-aloud now reads the page instead of everything on it.

Reading a comic aloud was close to unusable — reported as "sounds like they are talking in another language", which was fairly literal. Four things were wrong at once.

It read everything it found. Scanlation credits, watermarks, links and page numbers were all spoken as if they were dialogue. Worst of all, sound effects: scanlations leave Japanese onomatopoeia in romaji, so the voice was earnestly reading out "gogogogo" and "zawa zawa". Those are gone, along with text that comes back as garbage because the page is set in Japanese.

It read the page in the wrong order. Two speech bubbles side by side almost never sit at exactly the same height, and a few pixels of difference was enough to split them apart — so the voice read the top half of one bubble, then the top half of the other, then the bottoms. Bubbles are grouped into rows properly now.

It ignored right-to-left. Japanese comics read right to left and the app already has a page-by-page (RTL) mode, but the voice always went left first, so every exchange on the page came out backwards.

It read like a robot. Comic lettering is set in capitals, which makes speech engines spell short words out letter by letter. Words split across two lines with a hyphen were read as two words. Every fragment got a full stop after it, including ones already ending in "?" or "!".

Care has been taken not to swing too far the other way: a drawn-out shout like "NOOOO!" is dialogue and still gets read, lines like "I'll translate it" or "JOIN US!" are not credits, and a caption reading "1985" is a time skip, not a page number.

If a run of pages genuinely has no readable text, read-along now stops and tells you, instead of silently flipping through the chapter.
